request.spec:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Record every change to the sheet in the audit file, one line per change, appended in the order
the changes happen:
PERSON_ADDED name=<name> grade=<grade>, PERSON_EDITED name=<name> grade=<grade>,
CLAIM_ADDED person=<name> amount=<amount> date=<date>, and CLAIM_EDITED with the same fields.
Every line starts with the event, then sheet=<sheet id> and by=<signed-in user>, then the fields
in the order given, separated by single spaces. Amounts are written exactly as the screen shows
them (two decimals) and dates as yyyy-mm-dd. A change that is refused, by any rule now or later,
writes no line and changes nothing.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Every change to a sheet now writes one line to the audit file, and all 4 tests in the acceptance spec pass under `bin/e2e`. The change is server-side only; the front end didn't need anything.

- **Lines written:** `PERSON_ADDED` and `PERSON_EDITED` (with `name=` and `grade=`), and `CLAIM_ADDED` and `CLAIM_EDITED` (with `person=`, `amount=` and `date=`). Each one starts with the event, then `sheet=` and `by=`. Amounts have two decimals, as on screen, and dates are yyyy-mm-dd.
- **Refused changes write nothing:** a line is written only after the database commit succeeds (via a new `recordOnCommit` method in `Audit.java`). So a change refused by any rule, now or later — a bad amount, a duplicate name, a missing record, or a commit failure — leaves no line.
- **Who made the change:** the person and claim services now receive the signed-in user so they can fill in `by=`. The controllers already had it and now pass it through.

Things to be aware of:
- An edit is logged even if nothing changes. The tests expect this: setting a grade to the value it already has still writes `PERSON_EDITED`.
- A claim edit is logged when only its note changes. The line then looks the same as before because the note isn't one of the logged fields.
- If two users change the sheet at almost the same moment, lines follow the order the changes commit. Two near-simultaneous commits could, in rare cases, have their lines swapped. The tests run one change at a time, so they don't cover this.

The main changes are in `PersonService.java` and `ClaimService.java`.
